Detects restricted apps and optional YouTube Shorts playback during an active commitment

MIZAN uses this accessibility service to detect when a restricted app enters the foreground during an active commitment and, if you explicitly enable YouTube Shorts restriction, to recognize active YouTube Shorts player screens so MIZAN can navigate back automatically. MIZAN only reads minimal in-memory UI structure cues while YouTube Shorts restriction is active, never captures screenshots, never logs keystrokes, and never stores or uploads watch history, search queries, video titles, or comments.

• MIZAN uses Android VPN permission strictly for local on-device DNS filtering.
• Android allows only one active VPN at a time; enabling MIZAN may conflict with or displace another active VPN.
• Filtering is domain-based only — not HTTPS URL-path or page-content filtering.
• Encrypted DNS (Android Private DNS / DoT and browser DNS-over-HTTPS / DoH), hard-coded IPs, and proxies can circumvent local DNS filtering. Some banking or DRM apps also restrict access whenever any Android VPN is active.
• Ordinary browsing traffic is NOT routed through a remote MIZAN server; allowed queries forward to your active network's IPv4 or IPv6 DNS resolvers.
• Shared domains (such as shared CDNs) can cause legitimate services to become inaccessible.

MIZAN helps you set voluntary, calm boundaries on your own terms — without feeds, guilt, accounts, or tracking.

To detect restricted apps entering the foreground and measure foreground usage, Android requires you to manually enable MIZAN in Accessibility Settings. You can also optionally grant Usage Access to reconcile historical usage intervals locally, and optionally grant local VPN permission if you choose DNS-based website filtering. MIZAN never reads screen text, typed input, or screenshots, and never stores or uploads DNS query history.

Local preferences, privacy guarantees, and enforcement service health.

A trusted partner or your own future self can configure a local 4–8 digit PIN. MIZAN stores only a salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hash sealed with Android Keystore (AES-256-GCM) in no-backup storage. This is a voluntary deterrent, not tamper-proof device administration.
Start a calm 24-hour cooling-off timer before lifting commitment restrictions or clearing an Accountability PIN locally. You can cancel anytime, or complete deactivation once 24 hours have elapsed.
Honest limitation: This cooling-off period is a voluntary deterrent. Android never allows an ordinary app to block OS uninstall, force-stop, safe mode, ADB, or factory reset.
Update Social Media dataset on Wi-Fi only

WorkManager schedules Social Media updates on unmetered Wi-Fi when enabled (or any connected network when disabled). Adult Content updates are allowed on both Wi-Fi and cellular networks. Remote feeds remain disabled until a vetted HTTPS source and pinned ECDSA public key are configured; cached datasets and custom domains always filter offline.

DNS filtering limitations: Private DNS (DoT), browser DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH), IPv6-only routes, proxies, hard-coded IPs, and another active VPN can bypass or conflict with local DNS filtering; some banking apps also restrict connections while any VPN is active.

MIZAN stores all commitments, rules, and preferences exclusively in local Room and DataStore storage (excluded from cloud backup). MIZAN never stores DNS query history or browsing logs, and includes zero accounts, cloud sync, analytics, ads, or remote servers.

App restriction and live foreground timing require manual Accessibility Service opt-in. Optional Usage Access enables local interval reconciliation, and optional local VPN authorization enables on-device DNS domain filtering.
MIZAN is exempt from aggressive system battery throttling, helping Accessibility and local VPN enforcement remain stable across idle periods.

Block YouTube Shorts while keeping normal YouTube accessible
Automatically returns out of active YouTube Shorts (including shared Shorts links) while Home, Search, Subscriptions, channel pages, comments, and normal long-form videos stay available.

• Detection combines multiple in-memory UI structure cues inside YouTube to distinguish the active Shorts player from Home, Search, or normal videos.\n• Privacy: Inspection runs strictly in memory only when enabled in an active commitment. MIZAN never stores, logs, or uploads video titles, search queries, comments, or watch history.\n• Honest limitation: Future YouTube app updates can change layout structure and affect detection reliability. This feature uses Android Accessibility permission to perform a Back navigation and is best-effort rather than tamper-proof.
